SddAmplifyObservability.keywords: observability, amplify, logs, metrics, traces, alerts, slo, dashboards, sdd-amplify-observability
SddAmplifyObservability.Mission:
Make observability a set of design decisions in a scope spec under discovery — logs, metrics, traces, alerts — instead of an afterthought sprinkled at execution time. Loaded lazily by the discovery interview's triage when the scope has an operational runtime (service, worker, long-lived process); inherits the session core — not repeated here.
Input — the scope spec draft + interview context. Output — ordinary flat requirement entries in the canonical Requirements section + follow-up items on the discovery interview map. Out of scope: dashboard layouts and vendor configuration — detailed material belongs in Architecture or one referenced supporting section only when genuinely needed.
SddAmplifyObservability.BeliefState:
Inherited from the loading directive (already in context): QUESTION_FORMAT
An amplification opens with a ready answer, not a questionnaire. FIRST assemble a complete defaults package — the decisions live products of this class actually ship with (run a short targeted research pass when class practice is uncertain, grounded in the scope's intent) — and present it as ONE accept-or-edit reply: the operator takes everything with one word or edits by item number. Ask via the AskUserQuestion / multi-question tool when available; fallback `QUESTION_FORMAT`. Deep-dive questions open only for topics the operator explicitly marks deep-dive; every untouched topic keeps its default. An accepted default is a real decision — record it like one.
Every non-obvious decision → a Decision Log entry in `DECISION_LOG_ENTRY_FORMAT` — one line, the expanded part in parentheses: `-DL-N — (почему: …; отвергнуто: …; риск: …)`; IDs are stable. Non-obvious only (`AX_DECISION_LOG_NON_OBVIOUS`): a pick already recorded in the spec's own tables is never duplicated as a DL row. Which decisions qualify and which Decision Log receives the entry are specified per directive.
Raw `console.*` is forbidden. Use the shared logger from `#logger`: `logger[level](message, detail?)`. Levels: `debug` / `info` / `warn` / `error`. One or two arguments: first is a string message, second (when needed) is a `detail` object. **NEVER serialize objects into the message string.** Pseudo-loggers (`const logger = console`) forbidden.
The shared logger is the only sink that can be re-targeted (transport, redaction, sampling) without editing call-sites; raw `console` breaks agent-readable structure.
Logs at entry points, important branches, external I/O / mutations, catch blocks. Loops logged in aggregate, NOT per iteration. In `catch`: ALWAYS `logger.error` with Trace-Prefix and context, then recover via `throw` or `return fail()` per `AX_CATCH_LOG_RECOVER`. Intent-driven density yields a readable story-line; per-iteration spam drowns real signals.
Alert on operator-visible symptoms — SLO burn, error rate, saturation, staleness — and page a human only for actionable conditions; cause-level signals stay on dashboards. Every alert names its threshold, its severity, and the first response action. An alert nobody acts on is noise debt: delete it or demote it.
SddAmplifyObservability.HaltConditions: | 🛑 ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_NO_RUNTIME_SURFACE` | Triage misfired: no operational runtime (pure library — observability belongs to the consumer) — report and return control | | `H_OPERATOR_REJECTS_DEFAULTS` | Operator declines the whole defaults package and skips deep-dive — leave the spec untouched |

Step.Goal: Assemble the observability defaults package for this product class.
Step.Action: From the spec draft, list the operational surfaces: entry points, external I/O, queues, long operations. No runtime surface → `H_NO_RUNTIME_SURFACE`. Per `AX_AMPLIFY_DEFAULTS_FIRST`, draft one observable outcome per relevant signal: logs (structure + levels per `AX_STRUCTURED_LOGGING`, density per `AX_LOG_DENSITY`), metrics (RED for request paths / USE for resources — the minimal set answering «жив ли сервис и где болит»), traces (propagation boundaries + sampling), alerts (symptom → threshold → severity → first action, per `AX_ALERTS_ON_SYMPTOMS`) — grounded in what live products of this class ship; short targeted research when class practice is uncertain. A signal with no operational decision is not an entry.

Step.Goal: One accept-or-edit gate; deep-dive only on explicit pick.
Step.Action: Present the package as ONE reply per `AX_AMPLIFY_DEFAULTS_FIRST` (AskUserQuestion when available, else `QUESTION_FORMAT`); each signal accept / edit / deep-dive. Deep-dive topic map: logs → metrics → traces → alerts → SLO linkage. Untouched signals keep their defaults. STOP.

Step.Goal: Write the agreed outcomes as current-format requirements.
Step.Action:
Use the Requirements section's embedded grammar; do not preload a separate format. Continue the spec's next unused sequential `-REQ-` IDs. Write one ordinary flat entry per accepted observable outcome, with modality class, behaviour sentence, and short `Constraint`, `Verification`, and `Trace` lines. Never create `### Observability`, another topic heading, or a table inside Requirements.
If the existing Requirements section is legacy split/topic format, read it as input and migrate the whole section to flat entries in this already-approved edit; preserve every still-valid outcome and do not leave a mixed representation or ask for a second approval. An SLO/telemetry/alert matrix belongs in Architecture by default, or in one explicitly named supporting section outside Requirements only when the detail is genuinely needed; link it from `Trace`. Non-default picks and notable accepted defaults → Decision Log per `AX_DECISION_LOG_REQUIRED`. Unresolved topics → discovery interview map, not vague requirements. Return control to the interview.
